text: . On World Elephant Day, Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav, today said that Project Elephant reflects India’s commitment to protecting elephants, conserving their habitats and promoting harmonious coexistence between elephants and communities. In a social media post, Mr Yadav said that under Project Elephant, various measures are being implemented, including early warning systems and AI-based alerts to keep communities informed, solar-powered fences and trenches to protect people and elephants, and timely compensation for crop losses suffered by farmers. He added that the railways are also adopting warning signals, AI-based solutions and speed restrictions in critical corridors to prevent elephant deaths. The Minister also said that the government is promoting education and awareness to encourage communities to live in harmony with elephants.

. Somali pirates have hijacked two ships in four days, raising concerns that piracy is making a major comeback in waters off Somalia and Yemen amid growing regional instability. The latest incidents include the seizure of the Cameroon-flagged M/V LUTUF off Somalia’s Puntland coast and the hijacking of the Eritrean-flagged SIBU 1 tanker off Yemen. The LUTUF was reportedly carrying Turkish weapons and equipment bound for a military training facility in Mogadishu. The LUTUF’s 10-member crew included six Indians, one Turkish national, one Georgian and two Serbian security guards. Eight pirates reportedly took the vessel toward the Nugaal coast near Garmaal in Puntland’s Dangoroyo district.Somali officials said, six ships are currently being held by pirates, including the two seized this week, with more than 100 crew members being held hostage across those vessels. More than 17 piracy-related incidents were documented across Somali waters and the Gulf of Aden during the first five months of the year, including the hijacking of at least three commercial ships and five dhow boats. Experts say regional conflict, economic difficulties for fishermen and reduced maritime security are contributing to the resurgence. Somali piracy previously peaked around 2010, when hundreds of vessels were seized and shipping companies and insurers faced billions of dollars in losses.

. India’s foreign exchange reserves rose by 9.90 billion US dollars (USD) to 716.9 billion US dollars during the week ended August 14.According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 7.2 billion USD to 581.85 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves added 2.67 billion USD to 111.41 billion US dollars. Country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund was up by five million USD to around 4.89 billion USD. Special Drawing Rights decreased by five million USD to 18.74 billion USD.

. Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that saree is not merely a piece of attire, rather a magnificent symbol of Indian culture. The Minister said this in a video message during Saree Shastra in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat underlined the mastery of wearing one saree in multiple ways, the craft of designing and weaving a single saree in diverse styles. Highlighting the tradition of representing culture through sarees, he said that exhibitions and events like this help spread awareness about India’s tradition of wearing and weaving sarees, and understanding which saree suits which occasion far and wide.Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse said that the exhibition serves as a prime example of presenting diverse states and culture through sarees. The Minister said that the exhibition brings together artists from across the country and aims to present their work through the medium of the saree. He said, it reflects the country’s rich culture, which is being conveyed through saree craftsmanship.Saree Shastra is a three-day exhibition to honour the women who weave, preserve and wear sarees. The event reimangines the saree as one of India’s most enduring cultural artefact.

. India will host the 12th BRICS Communications Ministers Meeting in Pune tomorrow. The meeting will be chaired by Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia. It will bring together Communications Ministers and senior representatives from BRICS member countries to deliberate on strengthening cooperation in Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs), digital transformation, innovation and resilient digital infrastructure.The theme of the meeting is Innovate, Cooperate and Transform (ICT) for a Resilient Future. The event will provide a platform for BRICS member countries to exchange views on emerging technologies, digital public infrastructure, future networks, cybersecurity, capacity building and inclusive digital connectivity. The deliberations will also focus on advancing practical cooperation and sharing best practices to support digital transformation across BRICS countries and the wider Global South.

. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey has warned that any attempt to manipulate or defame the newly introduced Closing Auction Session, CAS, will be dealt with sternly.Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of an event organised by FICCI in Mumbai, Mr Pandey said, SEBI can detect manipulation under CAS more easily than under the earlier Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) system. He said, participation in CAS is improving, particularly among mutual funds and proprietary traders.SEBI introduced CAS on 3rd of this month to improve transparency and prevent market manipulation. Under the system, buy and sell orders are pooled during a designated period near the end of trading and matched through an auction process.Mr Pandey said, SEBI has not observed any manipulation in CAS so far and maintained that the new system is a major reform that is here to stay.

. In badminton, the fifth-seeded Indian pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty defeated Junaidi Arif and Roy King Yap of Malaysia in the pre-quarterfinals men’s doubles match at the BWF World Championships 2026 in New Delhi. The Indian pair had lost the first game 21-23 but bounced back to win the second and third games 21-19, 21-17 in a close encounter. The duo will now face third seeds Liang Wei Keng and Wang Chang of China in the quarterfinals.Earlier in the day, India’s women’s doubles duo of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand stormed into the quarterfinals of the World Championships. The Indian pair produced a commanding performance to defeat seventh seeds Rin Iwanaga and Kie Nakanishi of Japan in straight games, 21-16, 21-12. They will now face fourth seeds Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian of China in the quarterfinal.Meanwhile, former World champion P V Sindhu lost to third seed Wang Zhi Yi in the women’s singles pre-quarter-final match. Sindhu had lost the first game 11-21 but clawed back in the second game 21-15. However, she lost in the third game 17-21 in a closely contested match.Indian prodigy Ayush Shetty also lost to Indonesia’s Alwi Farhan in men’s singles round of 16. The Indian shuttler lost the match 19-21, 11-21. Meanwhile, the Indian mixed doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto also lost to China’s Guo Xin Wa and Chen Fang Hui 16-21, 5-21.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has lauded West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for handing over 1,129 acres of land to the Border Security Force (BSF) and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) for fencing along the India-Bangladesh border in the state within 45 days of the new government coming to power. He said the request for the land required for the border fence had been pending since 2014. Mr Shah was speaking while attending a programme at the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) Frontier Headquarters in the Ranidanga area of Siliguri in West Bengal yesterday.The Home Minister said completing border fencing is crucial to stopping infiltration and protecting national security. He said the government will continue its zero-tolerance policy towards illegal immigration. He said the process of identifying, removing and deporting illegal immigrants will be strictly followed. He also said that demographic changes would be strictly prevented.Highlighting the strategic importance of the Siliguri Corridor, also known as the ‘Chicken Neck’, Mr Shah said it is vital for the security of the Northeast and the country. He said the corridor, which connects the Northeast with the rest of the country and is bordered by three countries — Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh — will be protected by a triangular grid of Army posts in Chopra, Dhubri and Kishanganj. On the occasion, he laid foundation stones for infrastructure worth around 189 crore rupees and inaugurated several other projects.Union Home and Cooperation Minister also inaugurated a six-day awareness exhibition on the three new criminal laws, including the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, at Kawakhali Maidan in Siliguri.Addressing the gathering, Mr Shah said the three new criminal laws will provide greater security to citizens. He announced that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita has now been fully implemented in the state and said justice will be ensured within three years of the filing of an FIR. Mr Shah said the new criminal laws, which make extensive use of technology and forensic science, are aimed at ensuring speedy, timely and victim-centric justice. He said the judicial system will be transformed with “three Ts: Technology, Transparency and Timeline”.He said the BJP government under Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari implemented the new laws within three days of assuming office, fulfilling its promise of establishing trust, not fear. He appealed to the people of North Bengal to visit the exhibition. The Home Minister also urged people associated with the justice system, law enforcement and policing in the state to visit the exhibition and familiarise themselves with the new laws.On the occasion, Mr Shah also inaugurated the newly constructed Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate building and a 20-bed drug addiction treatment centre at North Bengal Medical College and Hospital.

. In the BWF Badminton World Championships, the Indian women’s doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand will take on top seeds Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning of China in the semifinals at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi today.The Indian duo stormed into the semifinals yesterday, defeating fourth seeds Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian of China 16-21, 21-15, 21-13. With this victory, Treesa and Gayatri have assured India of a coveted medal at the prestigious championship. Treesa and Gayatri also became only the second Indian women’s doubles duo to win a World Championships medal. Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa were the first Indian combination to achieve this feat when they clinched the bronze in London 15 years ago.India’s women’s doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand have expressed happiness after securing their place in the semifinals of the BWF Badminton World Championships in New Delhi. Talking to the media, the Indian pair said they were delighted to convert their hard-fought victory into a semifinal berth. However, they stressed that the journey does not end here, with more crucial matches still to come in the tournament. Treesa and Gayatri also thanked the home crowd for its support, saying that the energy and positive vibes from the stands gave them an added boost on court.Earlier in the day, the Indian men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty crashed out of the tournament after losing to China’s Liang Wei Keng and Wang Chang. The Indian duo went down to the fourth-seeded Chinese pair in straight games, 18-21, 9-21, in the quarterfinals.

. In Badminton, India’s Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand have stormed into the women’s doubles semifinals of the BWF World Championships in New Delhi. The Indian duo displayed remarkable grit and fighting spirit, coming from a game down to overcome fourth seeds Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian of China 16-21, 21-15, 21-13. With this triumph, Treesa and Gayatri have assured India of a coveted medal at the prestigious championship. This will be India’s first medal in the women’s doubles event at the World Championships in 15 years.

. India and Nepal reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation on border management and security. The discussion took place during the 14th meeting of the India-Nepal Joint Working Group (JWG), which concluded in Dehradun yesterday. Joint Secretary (BM-I) in the Union Home Ministry, Pausumi Basu, led the Indian delegation at the meeting, while the Nepalese side was led by Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Home Affairs, Ananda Kafle.The Union Home Ministry, in a statement, said that during the two-day meeting, discussions covered addressing trans-border crime and criminal activities, strengthening and effective utilisation of border infrastructure, roads and railway networks, removal of encroachments, and maintenance of boundary pillars. The two sides also exchanged views on strengthening institutional coordination and capacity building across various sectors and agreed to sustain engagement in these areas.

. The BRICS Tourism Ministers’ Meeting, held under India’s Chairship, concluded yesterday with the unanimous adoption of the Jaipur Declaration, which provides a framework for strengthening tourism cooperation among BRICS member countries. The declaration outlines key areas of cooperation, including the use of artificial intelligence in tourism, sustainable tourism practices, skill development and seamless travel facilitation.The meeting was presided over by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in Jaipur, Rajasthan, and marked the culmination of the BRICS Tourism Track under India’s Chairship in 2026. The Tourism Track was taken forward under the theme, “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”Addressing the meeting, Mr Shekhawat said tourism will play an important role in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047 and has the potential to extend economic growth beyond major urban centres to towns, villages and remote regions. He said the sector creates opportunities for hotels and homestays, taxi operators, tourist guides, artisans, weavers, farmers, entrepreneurs and millions of families whose livelihoods are directly or indirectly linked to tourism. He highlighted India’s efforts to build a tourism ecosystem that is economically prosperous, environmentally responsible, technologically enabled and culturally authentic.The BRICS Tourism Ministers’ Communiqué 2026, also known as the Jaipur Declaration, reflects the work undertaken by the BRICS Tourism Working Group during India’s Chairship and focuses on four key priorities: Artificial Intelligence and Tourism; Sustainability and Responsible Tourism; Tourism Skilling and Capacity Building; and Tourism Exchanges and Seamless Travel Facilitation. The Ministers’ Communiqué recognises the potential of responsible, safe and human-centred artificial intelligence and digital technologies to transform the tourism sector. It supports cooperation in areas such as tourism planning, destination management, visitor services, multilingual communication and travel facilitation.The meeting was attended by representatives of nine BRICS member states. Ministerial participants included Gustavo Costa Feliciano, Minister of Tourism of Brazil; Reza Salehi Amiri, Iran’s Minister of Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Handicrafts; Patricia De Lille, South Africa’s Minister of Tourism; and Abdulla Bin Touq Al Marri, UAE Minister of Economy and Tourism. Heads of delegations from China, Ethiopia, Indonesia and Russia also attended the meeting.Speaking to the media after the BRICS Tourism Ministers’ Meeting, Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said the Jaipur Declaration adopted at the meeting will strengthen joint strategies and cooperation among BRICS countries and open new opportunities in tourism. He called for more effective use of Artificial Intelligence in the tourism sector. He stressed the need to promote responsible tourism and enhance skill development in the sector. Mr Shekhawat said the number of tourists visiting India has tripled over the past decade. He added that Jaipur is also expected to benefit significantly from these initiatives.On the sidelines of the ministerial meeting, India held bilateral discussions with Brazil, Iran, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates to further advance tourism cooperation.

. The Report of the Inquiry Committee investigating allegations concerning former Allahabad High Court Judge Yashwant Varma was tabled in both the Houses of Parliament. In the Lok Sabha, Secretary General Uttpal Kuma Singh tabled the Hindi and English versions of the Report of the Inquiry Committee constituted under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 as well as the Oral and documentary evidence recorded during the course of the inquiry. While in the Rajya Sabha, the report in this regard was tabled by Secretary General P C Mody.The Judges Inquiry Committee, investigating allegations concerning Yashwant Varma, had submitted its report to the Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in May this year. The Committee was constituted by Mr Birla on 12th of August last year to probe the allegations levelled against Justice Varma, after a sum of burnt cash was found at his official residence in New Delhi.

. Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Today took oath as the 23rd President of Bangladesh at Bangabhaban in Dhaka.The oath was administered by the Acting Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal. Mr. Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected President yesterday after defeating Oli Ahmed, who was backed by the Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance. He secured 255 votes against Mr. Ahmed’s 88 votes out of 343 valid votes cast in the presidential election held yesterday.The last presidential election in Bangladesh to be decided through voting in Parliament was held on October 8, 1991.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has highlighted the importance of preserving India’s cultural roots, noting that culture is a strong bond that unites the country.Addressing the Antar-Hriday Connect Malhar 2026 event in New Delhi, the Vice President called upon the youth, particularly Gen Z, to contribute towards reforming and strengthening the system with patience and responsibility.He underlined the importance of initiatives that expose young people to India’s diverse cultural traditions and strengthen their sense of belonging to the nation. The Vice President noted that India’s classical music traditions have survived for centuries because they have continuously evolved while retaining their essence. Further, he said music should be accessible to everyone as it brings peace and connects people across regions, languages and cultures.

. The Government today launched the National Campaign on Entrepreneurship- II’ under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) for another three months, from today till 21st of November this year.The Ministry of Rural Development said that the campaign will strengthen rural women’s entrepreneurship and will contribute to the vision of making six crore Lakhpati Didis.The extended phase of the campaign will focus on promoting entrepreneurship among Self Help Group (SHG) women across Farm and Non-Farm livelihoods, strengthening the community enterprise promotion cadre, promoting enterprise formalisation, expanding digital and e-commerce adoption, and strengthening producer groups and producer enterprises.The Ministry noted that the campaign has set an ambitious outcomes, including orientation of 50 thousand community cadres, entrepreneurship and livelihood training for five lakh SHG women, creation of a database of five lakh adolescent girls from SHG households, formalisation support for 50 thousand enterprises, strengthening membership of Producer Groups and Producer Enterprises by two lakh members, promotion of agro-ecological practices among 20 lakh women, and onboarding of 25 thousand SHG members on e-commerce platforms.

. India will host the BRICS Youth Ministers’ Meeting and the BRICS Sports Ministers’ Meeting in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. The BRICS Youth Ministers’ Meeting will be held today, while the BRICS Sports Ministers’ Meeting will take place tomorrow. The meetings will be chaired by Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, with Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse also participating.According to the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Youth Ministers’ Meeting will focus on strengthening cooperation in youth development and empowerment, with discussions on education, skill development, entrepreneurship, wellbeing and sustainable development. The Sports Ministers’ Meeting will bring together Sports Ministers and Heads of Delegation from the 11 BRICS member countries to reaffirm their shared commitment to strengthening cooperation in sports.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya has called for an accelerated and comprehensive talent identification roadmap to build India’s athlete pool for the 2036 Olympics. It came following Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s announcement of a nationwide sports talent hunt from the ramparts of the Red Fort.Chairing the 63rd Governing Body Meeting of the Sports Authority of India (SAI), Dr. Mandaviya emphasised that the groundwork for India’s sporting ambitions over the next decade must begin now. He said talent identification should cover the entire sporting pyramid, including schools, districts and colleges.The Minister underlined that the aim should be to build a comprehensive talent repository that can subsequently feed into sports schools and higher-level training systems. Dr. Mandaviya further emphasised the need to develop a public-private partnership model to expand the training ecosystem so that athletes identified through State and district-level talent hunts could be channelled to suitable academies for specialised training.He also underlined the important role of the corporate sector in expanding sports development through greater CSR participation and added that such partnerships would help augment the country’s training capacity beyond government-run facilities, creating a wider network of academies for athletes.The Governing Body approved the establishment of the National Coach Accreditation Board, which will provide a more structured framework for coach accreditation and development. The Ministry noted that the body also approved a proposed amendment to the recruitment rules for appointment to the post of Assistant Coach (Pay Level-6) on deputation basis in SAI.

. A US charter aircraft carrying eight people crashed at a remote radar site in western Alaska, killing everyone on board. According to the US military, the crash occurred at the Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site Airport, about 725 kilometres west of Anchorage, Alaska, last night.The Federal Aviation Administration said the Cessna 441 that had taken off from Anchorage was headed towards Cape Newenham when it crashed. The aircraft was reportedly carrying personnel travelling to the Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site. US Air Force Lt. Gen. Robert Davis, commander of Alaskan Command, described the incident as a devastating loss for the military and local communities.

. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the National Teachers’ Awards on 48 school teachers on the 5th of next month at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi.The Education Ministry said school teachers have been selected through a three-stage selection process at the District, State and National levels by the Department of School Education and Literacy. The 48 selected school teachers are from 27 States, 7 Union Territories and 6 organisations of the Central Government. Of the 48 selected school teachers, 26 are male and 22 are female.The Ministry said online self-nominations from eligible teachers for the National Teachers’ Awards 2026 were invited from 15th June to 20th July this year through the Ministry of Education’s portal, nationalawardstoteachers.education.gov.in. The event will be telecast live on Doordarshan and the SWAYAM PRABHA channels of the Ministry of Education.

. India’s Kajal Dhochak has won her second consecutive U20 World Wrestling Championship title. She clinched the women’s 76-kilogram gold medal with a commanding 7-0 victory over China’s Jingru Sun in the final.In the 72-kilogram category, India’s Tanu Sharma put up a determined fight against Japan’s Chisato Yoshida in the final but lost 3-5 to settle for silver. In the 62-kilogram category, Savita also won a silver medal after losing to Japan’s Sakura Onishi by technical superiority, 2-12. India’s Mansi Lather is in contention for gold in the 68-kilogram category. She will face China’s Chenling Song in the final.In the 59-kilogram repechage round, Komal will take on Spain’s Rosa Molina Rodriguez.India’s Greco-Roman wrestlers finished the competition without a medal. The men’s freestyle events will begin later today and conclude on Sunday.

. Ace Indian javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra finished second at the Lausanne Diamond League with a season-best throw of 88.05 metres, just nine centimetres behind Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, who won with 88.14 metres.The two-time Olympic medallist’s 88.05-metre throw marked a strong return to the 88-metre range after a difficult start to the 2026 season. Pathirage reclaimed the lead with his third attempt, and neither athlete could improve their marks in the remaining rounds.Anderson Peters finished third with 86.69 metres, while Keshorn Walcott took fourth with 83.71 metres. The result extends Chopra’s wait for a victory since his win at the Neeraj Chopra Classic in Bengaluru in July 2025. However, his season-best performance in Lausanne will be a major boost.

. Iran has warned that it will give a strong response to any new threats from the United States. The chief of staff of Iran’s Armed Forces, Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi, said, the Islamic Republic’s reaction would be broad and decisive.The warning came after Washington announced plans to impose what it described as the toughest financial sanctions in history, aimed at putting pressure on the Iranian leadership. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi rejected the economic threats made against his country, saying that such failed policies will stir more hostility among Iranians and bring more failures.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to announce details of the new sanctions on Monday. US President Donald Trump has also warned of economic consequences for countries providing any form of support to Iran.Iran’s Armed Forces Chief of Staff, Major General Ali Abdollahi, said the country’s response to any new threats would be broad and decisive. He said Iran’s armed forces were prepared across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace to respond to what he called enemy threats.

. The Trump administration has imposed new sanctions on nine Cuban state-owned firms in the construction, mining and metals sectors, while tightening restrictions on US citizens doing business with Cuban state entities.The latest measures follow Havana’s rejection of the curbs after several American citizens returning from events associated with Fidel Castro’s 100th birthday were briefly detained at Miami airport, as the island continues to grapple with a deteriorating economic downturn.According to the US Treasury and State departments, the newly announced restrictions  target leaders of the Cuban Institute of Friendship with the Peoples (ICAP). US Secretary of State Marco Rubio asserted that the organisation is accountable for sponsoring “a vast subversive network in the United States aimed at identifying, cultivating, and radicalising” Americans.

. Ministry of Finance has said that Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) have recorded strong growth in credit delivery during the financial year 2025-26.The Ministry said the performance of RRBs under the Reserve Bank of India’s Priority Sector Lending framework remained strong during the year. However, the gross loans outstanding of RRBs increased by 10.3 percent from nearly 5 lakh 24 thousand crore rupees in financial year 2024- 25 to over 5 lakh 78 thousand crore rupees in 2025-26.The Ministry said that agriculture and allied activities remained the largest component of the RRB credit portfolio, with outstanding credit of 3.78 lakh crore rupees constituting 77 percent of the total Priority Sector Lending.Credit to the MSME sector stood at around 67 thousand crore rupees, reaffirming the pivotal role of RRBs in supporting rural entrepreneurship and employment generation.The Ministry said, the financial performance of RRBs during the year 2025-26 highlights sustained expansion in rural credit, strong alignment with national development priorities and continued support to farmers, micro-enterprises and other underserved segments.

. The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) has achieved a major milestone in its nationwide mission-mode drive for Mandatory Biometric Updates, completing more than two crore biometric updates for school children across the country. The special drive, initiated in September last year, has now covered over one lakh 56 thousand schools, enabling school children to complete their Aadhaar biometric. Electronics and IT Ministry said that this has helped Mandatory Biometric Updates service to reach children directly at their schools, making the process more accessible and convenient for crores of students.Aadhaar enrolment for children below five years captures demographic information and a photograph, while fingerprints and iris biometrics are not captured at that age as these biometrics are still developing. Mandatory Biometric Updates helps ensure that the child’s Aadhaar continues to have updated biometric information. The Biometric updates are required when a child attains the age of 5 years and again at 15 years. To encourage timely completion and make the service more accessible, UIDAI had waived the charges for  children in the 7 to 15 years age group from 1st October 2025, for a period of one year. The Ministry said that lack of Biometric Updates in Aadhaar may lead to difficulties while carrying out authentication for receiving benefits under various Government schemes, registering in competitive and university examinations.

. Union Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth has described the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment (MMDR) Bill, 2026, as a historic step that will change the fortunes and landscape of mineral-rich states like Jharkhand. Addressing a press conference in Ranchi today, he said the Bill will strengthen the interests of states and contribute to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.Mr. Seth said nearly 90 percent of mineral revenue will continue to go to the states, rejecting opposition claims that the interests of states have been compromised. He said the Bill will help curb illegal mining and mineral theft through a zero-tolerance approach, while a transparent and stable tax regime will boost investment, production and employment.He said mineral revenue in Jharkhand has increased from around 4,662 crore rupees before 2014 to nearly 33,494 crore rupees in 2025-26, an increase of around 618 percent.Mr. Seth said India has sufficient coal resources and stressed that faster mining, prevention of illegal mining and simplified procedures can reduce imports and strengthen the country’s self-reliance.

. Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr L Murugan today said Government has established a Fact Check Unit in Press Information Bureau to mitigate fake news related to its programmes and policies. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, DR Murugan informed that the Fact Check Unit verifies claims relating to Government Ministries, Departments, PSUs and other Central Government organisations through a structured fact-checking process. It disseminates verified information through various platforms.The MoS further stated that Doordarshan and Akashvani further disseminate verified information through their news bulletins, programmes and digital platforms. DD News follows a multi-layered editorial mechanism involving rigorous fact-checking, cross-verification through multiple credible sources and editorial scrutiny before broadcast. PIB Fact Check content is regularly integrated into Doordarshan and Akashvani news and digital platforms to counter misinformation and false narratives.PIB, as the principal information dissemination agency of the Government, facilitates timely, credible and accurate communication in different forms through various media platforms. Prasar Bharati plays a key role in fulfilling the mandate of public service broadcasting. Information is disseminated in multiple languages, including regional languages and dialects, using various platforms.

. The unincorporated establishments in the non-agriculture sector continued their growth momentum in the first quarter of this financial year. Despite global uncertainties, the sector grew 9.2 per cent year-on-year for the April to June quarter, according to the Quarterly Bulletin of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (QBUSE) released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation today.The estimated number of establishments increased to 8.67 crore in this period. Employment in the unincorporated non-agricultural sector reached 13.70 crore, with the other services sector emerging as a key driver, recording employment growth of more than 21 per cent. This was followed by the manufacturing sector, which registered growth of 10.06 per cent in the estimated number of establishments and 6.60 per cent in the estimated workforce.However, the unincorporated trade sector recorded a year-on-year decline of 7.88 per cent in the estimated number of establishments and 10.29 per cent in the estimated workforce.The urban sector outperformed the rural sector in employment growth, registering a year-on-year growth of over 12 per cent, compared with 0.70 per cent growth in rural sector. The report further highlighted that women accounting for more than 30 per cent of total employment in the sector.

. Vice President of Financial Action Task Force Vivek Aggarwal today highlighted the important role of regulatory bodies in strengthening collective efforts to combat illicit finance.He said this during a meeting with Executive Directors of the International Financial Services Centres Authority Dipesh Shah and K. Mahipal Reddy held in New Delhi.The discussions also focused on key regulatory and supervisory initiatives, emerging risks, and measures to strengthen compliance and effectiveness in combating money laundering and terrorist financing.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in negative territory today. The Sensex declined 493 points or 0.63 per cent to close at 77,235. The Nifty slipped 133 points or 0.55 per cent to settle at 24,155. In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell 0.4 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index remained unchanged.Earlier, the markets opened lower amid weak global cues. Both indices remained under pressure and traded in a range-bound manner through most of the session. However, towards the fag end of the session, the markets extended their decline amid selling pressure ahead of the weekly expiry of Nifty futures and options contracts.In the Sensex pack, 22 out of 30 companies registered losses. Among the top underperformers, Asian Paints shed 2.4 per cent, Infosys dropped two per cent and HCL Tech lost 1.9 per cent. In contrast, Axis Bank added 0.9 per cent, Power Grid gained 0.7 per cent and Mahindra and Mahindra edged up half a per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 21 out of 28 sectors ended with losses. Among the top laggards, Focused IT declined 1.8 per cent, Information Technology dropped 1.7 per cent and Realty lost 1.3 per cent. In contrast, Midsmall Private Banks Quality Tilt advanced 0.3 per cent, Hospitals as well as Healthcare increased by a quarter of a per cent, and Auto added 0.2 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,384 companies declined, 1,930 advanced and 216 remained unchanged.

. Young workers are driving the growth of India’s formal employment, with 79 per cent of new Universal Account Numbers generated during 2025-26 belonging to people aged between 18 and 30 years. According to a report, Pulse FY2026, more than 57,000 new UANs were generated during the year. The 21 to 25 age group accounted for over 35 per cent of these accounts, making it the largest group entering formal employment.The report also found that nearly 59 per cent of new Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation subscribers in 2024-25 were aged between 18 and 25, highlighting the growing contribution of young workers to India’s formal economy.According to the report, nearly 64,000 apprenticeship contracts were facilitated under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme. The automotive sector accounted for more than 51 per cent of these contracts. Women accounted for nearly 28 per cent of new UANs generated during 2025-26 and received 26 per cent of apprenticeship contracts.The report also highlighted the growing importance of smaller cities, with nearly 69 per cent of the workforce deployed across tier-II and tier-III cities. It said India’s organised workforce is also becoming more educated. Around 96 per cent of workers have completed at least Class 10, while 61 per cent have completed Class 12 or higher. About 30 per cent hold graduate or postgraduate qualifications.
